On Tue, Nov 18, 2008 at 8:47 AM, Bin liu <binl...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi Guys,
>
> Any clue about the questions listed below?
>
> I tried to install on another machine which doesn't have direct link to the
> internet, so I mirrored all the R2.8 and bioconductor packages on that
> machine, and installed R packages from the local repository, I mirrored all
> the aroma packages to the machine as well, using R CMD INSTALL, and got
> error messages with all the latest version packages, saying the gz file are
> not in gzip format. So I unzip the zip file, recompress the packages to the
> gz file, and R CMD INSTALL seemed fine, but my gz file couldn't find the any
> dependence file, and gave error message about some packages was built for
> i386-pc-mingw32".

o) What is you sessionInfo()?

o) Is this an independent problem of what you previously reported or a follow?

o) Do you have a successful installation of aroma.affymetrix anywhere?
Are you experience a problem only with the new version or is this
your first time you install the package?

o) What is "the local repository"?

o) Is this replated only to aroma.* and R.* packages, or also
BioC/CRANpackages? If your problem is not specific to aroma.*/R.*
packages, please try to do what you want to do with a few CRAN and/or
BioC packages first. If that does not work, turn to the R manuals
(see help.start()) and the r-help mailing list for help
[http://www.r-project.org/]

o) Are you trying to install *.gz package on a Windows system, or
*.zip packages on *nix systems? Then, use the R manuals and the
r-help list.

o) Unless you really know what you're doing, a good rule of thumb is
to never ever do tricks like unzipping and rezipping to work around an
initial problem, especially not when it comes to installing R
packages.

o) You don't explain from where and how you downloaded and transferred
the problematic *.gz files. It is a common problem (not just in R)
that binary files get corrupted if downloaded using FTP via a *text*
and not *binary* transfer.

/Henrik
